pages.title: Follow Connections
pages.subtext: Not every connection works in both directions.
pages.cardText: Some roads are two-way. Others only allow travel in one direction. Graphs can model both.
pages.tipText: Classify graph direction and read neighbouring vertices.

pages.title: Two-way connections
pages.subtext: In an undirected graph, an edge can be used both ways.
pages.cardText: If A connects to B, then the same edge can be travelled from B to A.
pages.tipText: No arrowheads are required. A — B and B — A refer to the same undirected connection.

contentBox.text: Tap connected nodes to highlight the edge.

pages.title: One-way connections
pages.subtext: A directed edge has an arrow showing permitted movement.
pages.cardText: A directed connection from A to B does not necessarily allow B to A.
pages.tipText: Follow the arrowheads to see valid movement.

contentBox.text: Follow the arrows to see valid movement.

pages.title: Can you go backwards?
pages.subtext: Suppose the only directed edge is A → B.
pages.cardText: Which journey is guaranteed by this single edge?
pages.correctFeedback: Directed edges have a specified direction. Undirected edges work in both directions.
pages.incorrectFeedback: A directed edge only allows movement in the direction of the arrow (from A to B).

pages.title: Find the neighbours
pages.subtext: Adjacent vertices are linked by an edge.
pages.cardText: In the undirected diagram, A has direct edges to B and C, not D.
pages.tipText: Hint: follow only one edge away from A.

contentBox.text: Adjacent vertices linked by an edge.

pages.title: Graphs as lists
pages.subtext: A computer can store neighbours in an adjacency list.
pages.cardText:
A: B, C
B: A, C, D
C: A, B, D
D: B, C
pages.tipText: Lists store the vertices directly connected to each vertex; this example is undirected.

pages.title: Connections understood
pages.subtext: You can now reason about which moves are possible.
pages.cardText: Directed edges have a specified direction. Undirected edges work in both directions.
pages.tipText: For the example graph, neighbours of A are B and C. Adjacency does not require travelling multiple edges.
